title: Undependable
text:
I have tried to use this app over the last 4 years off and on without success. Has it ever worked for me? Yes. Has it worked for me when I really needed it to? No. Today is yet another example of absolute frustration with this app. I’m an insurance field adjuster who works remotely all over the country, often in areas with limited cell coverage. The area I’m in now is also remote but growing, meaning there’s plenty of new construction that won’t show up on Google Earth. The perfect solution is Hover right? Not so much. Today’s example has me scoping a large, cut up country McMansion that just got finished this year. I show up and you couldn’t ask for better views of every elevation as there’s no landscaping around the house at all - the perfect blank canvas for Hover.

I get my 9 shots plus 2 extra with recommended clear space and full view of every elevation and corner to corner, etc. Textbook shots. BUT… I only have one bar of reception. The app says proceed to submit if you’re all done, which I am/do, and here’s where the fun starts. A blue icon shows up that says “Uploading” and a warning not to leave the app while its doing so. Okay, so I stand at the back of my truck and wait. And wait. And wait some more. I’m hoping not to be late to my next 2 inspections but I don’t want to leave until I know I’ve got the shots the app needs. But there’s no progress bar letting me know how far along it’s going if at all, so I wait. Like an idiot. The iPad goes to auto sleep, but apparently that’s considered ‘leaving the app’ because it throws up a notification on the screen telling me to come back. Is the upload hosed? Who knows? There’s nothing to tell me it is or isn’t, so I finally head out to my next appointment hoping I get better reception for it to finish. I’m literally driving with the iPad on my lap and tapping the screen to keep it awake, but nothing ever changes. It just says “Uploading”. Is it though? How can you tell? You can’t. You’re just a schmuck staring at a motionless blue icon you hope will change. It doesn’t. It hasn’t and it’s been over 2 hours and 2 calls to support with the only other option being a manual submission of photos that were thankfully saved to my photo roll. Suggestion for the developers: implement a progress bar and similar to XM8 mobile, have a resilient offline mode of capturing photos and projects that isn’t dependent on a strong internet connection when one isn’t available.

This is often caused by an incorrect or expired SSL certificate. The most annoying shortfall is that it's clear that the photos you take, including the extra photos, aren't saved anywhere on your device. What's up with that? title: Right idea...but falls short in too many ways
text:
It’s okay for very basic early stage estimation. The accuracy vs other tools and lasers is off considerably. The VERY BIG MISSES are: pro version isn’t able to be shared with clients. That basically makes it useless as a tool to set you apart from others. Roofers will probably find it effective but at twice the cost of other measuring tools. 

The design feature falls FAR SHORT from a contractor’s needs. You can’t do simple design features like adding shutters or accent trim. The support team would do them for you but they’ve stopped that now without notice. This is a critical function for clients and it falls way short. 

I was excited. Have used it for 47 properties, which I think constitutes a thorough trial. But I’m going to another tool. They don’t seem to prioritize design improvements. I can’t hold up my value prop to my clients over a design tool. Live and learn I guess. 

It also doesn’t look as good as tools that cost very little to buy and don’t have the per project fees Hover does. And it doesn’t function very well on detail design.  The color pallets are way off too. 

The other very bad thing is that they only give you one design you can save. So you’ll need another tool on top of this one for sure. It’s basically just a measuring tool that gives you a +/-  5% measurement. The service team which seems to be nice people, didn’t know the pro limitations until I told them. That seems to me that someone in development launched the product too early and they couldn’t figure out how to deliver the obvious pro features that would make it worthwhile. 

I do mostly 4,000-10,000 sqft homes. What you get on those is worth $20-30, but it costs $116 per house. 

And they give you no storage so your work goes away after some time. 

Lastly, when using your phone to start the project, it won’t allow your camera to zoom in and out. So, if you don’t have a large yard with no trees, shrubs, etc within 40-50 feet of the house, it’s not worth using. 

Basically a super idea but it’s overpriced and under-equipped.

title: Neat tool, app still needs some work
text:
This is a very neat and powerful tool.  With 18 simple photos that included fences and other stuff in the way, it was able to give me an model that appears very close to what my house looks like.  Unfortunately, at least with the free homeowner version, you don’t get to see any measurements. I can’t verify the dimensions so I have no idea how accurate the model is.  

The app itself is a little clunky.  It’s too easy to hit the wrong BACK button and jump out of model space. In addition, I feel like I should be able to touch the feature I want to change instead of trying to find it in the menu.  For some reason doors also don’t appear in the menu so you can’t change those.

Lastly, the menu is brand based vs object/style based.  Because of that, you have to know what brand you want before you can even choose a color or style.  As a homeowner, my first concern isn’t brand but style and color.  Brand is secondary.

Overall, powerful tool but the interface still needs some tweaking.
